_comment: sets_3 regrouped: each team is one kind of robot (user, 2026-09-15).
team_1 is the three Ridgeback+UR5 arms, team_2 the three Jackal carriers,
team_3 the three Crazyflies. Nine robots, Merom_1_int, all spawned together.
Every robot is the one of the same name in sets_3 -- same model, same spawn
position, same scale, same _v4_prim -- and only its 'team' differs, so the
pair is a clean A/B on grouping alone: V4's trios (arm + carrier + drone)
against three single-kind teams.
What that changes, on the S1 routes: no team can move cargo by itself.
An arm marked base_locked_while_holding cannot drive while loaded, and
team_1 has no carrier to load onto; team_2 has no arm to lift with at all,
and neither does team_3 (the lift table gives notebook.n.01 to arm only, so
on v4_s1_v4_lh the drones cannot carry the cargo even though they fly).
So every leg of a route needs a cross-team handoff: a team_1 arm grasps,
load_onto a team_2 jackal, the jackal drives, a team_1 arm unload_from it
at the far end. That is expressible and permitted -- neither the room
listing nor load_onto/unload_from's reach gate knows about teams -- but it
is a coordination problem sets_3 does not pose, which is the point.
Positions are sets_3's and keep its geometry: everyone packed around the
centroid of living_room_0's largest free region, ground vehicles placed
nearest-to-centroid first, each Crazyflie hovering at z = 1.2 m directly
above the Jackal it shared a V4 station with. The drone is no longer that
Jackal's teammate, which costs nothing: a hovering drone and a ground robot
are different layers to the separation check.
Robots are listed team by team here. In sets_3 the name's ordinal is the
team number; here it indexes within the kind, since a team holds three of
one kind. Names, and therefore every id in a prompt, are unchanged.
Scales: ridgeback 0.5 and jackal 0.7 are the values v4_s1_v4_ll was verified
with (the staging USD says 1.0 / 0.5, unresolved); crazyflie 2.0 by decision.
